title: Capacity Concierge: proactive right-sizing workflow and utilization signals for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Dedicated often overprovision GPU capacity to avoid SLO violations and burst events. This drives outsized committed costs. Current tooling surfaces utilization but lacks a proactive, tenant-aware rightsizing workflow that combines throughput guarantees, autoscale policy tuning, and conservative headroom suggestions.

Goal: Build a 'Capacity Concierge' feature that: 1) computes tenant-level right-size recommendations (slots / GPUs / commit tiers) using time-series utilization, token throughput, and burst profiles; 2) exposes an explainable recommendation UI in Console with simulated cost delta and SLO risk; 3) provides autoscaling policy templates and one-click apply with rollback/canary; 4) ties to fleet controls so operators can accept, schedule, or auto-apply suggestions with audit logs.

Scope: telemetry pipeline changes, rightsizing algorithm, Console UX, apply path (API + backend), alerting for recommendation drift, rollout plan with canary, and docs for Solutions Engineers. Not in scope: billing contract renegotiation, cross-cluster live migration of tenants (post-MVP).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces per-tenant suggested commit size and slot allocation with confidence score and explanation for last 14 days
Console shows simulated monthly cost delta and p95 latency SLO breach probability for current vs recommended commit
One-click apply triggers a safe change: creates change request, schedules canary (5% traffic), monitors SLOs for 30m, auto-rolls back on regression
Autoscale policy templates (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) available for tenants with documented trade-offs
Telemetry dashboards updated with new signals: sustained_tokens_per_sec, burst_tail_probability, packing_efficiency, tenant_headroom_pct
Audit log entry created for every recommendation viewed / applied and stored for 90 days
Runbook for SRE and Solutions ENs describing failure modes and manual rollback steps exists in Confluence
Integration tests for recommendation engine deterministic behavior added to infra-test-suite
notes: Initial data exploration covered 100 Dedicated tenants (sample period: 2025-10 to 2026-01) — median utilization skewed by periodic batch workloads; see dashboard link
We will use existing token accounting + new 1m aggregation window. Avoid changing tenant-side SDKs.
Cost simulation uses current pricing model for Reserved GPU slots; include 5% buffer for quantization uncertainty
Privacy: do not include user prompt text in telemetry; only aggregate metrics are permitted per privacy policy
comments: 2026-02-03 // Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting notes — scope agreed with Product and SRE. Initial success metric: reduce committed spend by 12% across pilot tenants without >0.5% increase in SLO breaches.

2026-02-10 // Ravi Kapoor: Prototype rightsizer implemented (PR #6349). Uses rolling 1h windows and weighted burst factor. Produces candidate sizes and a confidence score from 0-1. Next: validate against historical episodes (replay).
2026-02-18 // Mei Chen (Product): Reviewed trade-offs — prefer conservative defaults for multitenant pools. Product requests ability to pin recommendations to 'never auto-apply' by customer opt-in.

2026-02-22 // Priya Nair (SRE): Raised concern about headroom pct computation. Proposed adding 'sustained_tokens_per_sec' and 'burst_tail_probability' signals and validating false-positive rollback rate <1%.
2026-03-01 // Ravi Kapoor: Telemetry pipeline change landed — new aggregations written to metrics.v2. Backfill job ran for pilot tenants (7d window). Dashboard updated.

2026-03-05 // Design review: Console mockups reviewed. Need simpler explanation for 'confidence' for non-technical customers. UX will show 'Why we recommend this' bullets (peak events, low packing, long idle windows).

2026-03-08 // QA: End-to-end test flakiness observed in canary rollback when spikes occur in first 10m. Mitigation: extend observation window to 30m and require both latency and error-rate checks before rollback decision.

2026-03-10 // Solutions Eng (Diego Alvarez): Approval to run pilot with 12 paid customers starting 2026-03-20. Requirement: opt-in and ability to preview impact and schedule change during maintenance windows.

2026-03-12 // Ravi Kapoor: Updated algorithm to include packing_efficiency factor to avoid recommending downsizes when tenant packing is suboptimal. This reduces false positives in mixed-workload pools.
